item.content:encoded:
Mount Kenya University has signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with Junge Zukunft gGmbH, a Berlin-based organisation in Germany, to strengthen international collaboration, promote ethical recruitment practices, and create structured professional pathways for eligible MKU students and graduates.

The MoU was signed on 26 October 2026 at the Vice-Chancellor’s Office, MKU Main Campus in Thika, by the MKU Vice-Chancellor and René Pernull and Kadir Kaan, Founders and Managing Directors of Junge Zukunft gGmbH.

The partnership seeks to facilitate ethical, transparent, and structured pathways for qualified MKU students and graduates (alumni) Bachelor of Social work  & administration, Early Childhood Development, Nursing, and Special Needs Education to access professional opportunities in Germany. The program is guided by a rigorous recruitment and selection process coordinated through the MKU Office of Career Services and Junge Zukunft gGmbH team, ensuring that candidates meet the agreed academic and professional requirements.

As part of the preparation for international placement, selected and eligible candidates will receive support in acquiring proficiency in the German language at the B2 level. This training will be facilitated by the MKU Centre for Professional Development, equipping participants with the necessary language skills to pursue professional opportunities in Germany.

The MoU will remain in force for five years, with recruitment exercises conducted twice annually. This structured approach is expected to provide eligible students and graduates with regular opportunities to explore international career pathways while ensuring that recruitment processes are transparent, responsible, and aligned with the partners’ shared objectives.

The partnership marks an important milestone in MKU’s commitment to expanding international collaborations, enhancing graduate employability, and connecting its graduates to global career opportunities. Through this collaboration, MKU and Junge Zukunft gGmbH look forward to fostering sustainable partnerships that benefit students, alumni, and the broader professional communities in Kenya and Germany.

item.content:encoded:
Mount Kenya University (MKU) has strengthened its commitment to practical, competency-based healthcare education through a partnership with Nakuru County Referral and Teaching Hospital (NCRTH) to expand clinical training opportunities for health sciences students.

The partnership was formalised through the signing of a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) between MKU, NCRTH and the Department of Health, establishing a framework for clinical attachments, internships and hands-on learning within a functional healthcare environment.

The hospital was represented by Santosh Davaraj, Hospital Director, Nakuru County Referral and Teaching Hospital, who joined the institutional leadership in advancing the partnership aimed at strengthening clinical training and healthcare education. The collaboration reflects the hospital’s commitment to supporting the training of future healthcare professionals by providing opportunities for practical learning, skills development and professional mentorship within a real healthcare setting.

Through the collaboration, MKU students will gain valuable practical experience in real patient-care settings, working under the guidance of experienced healthcare professionals. The exposure will enable learners to apply classroom knowledge, develop essential clinical competencies and prepare for the demands of professional healthcare practice.

The partnership underscores MKU’s commitment to producing competent, industry-ready graduates whose skills respond to the evolving needs of the healthcare sector. By bridging the gap between academic instruction and clinical practice, the collaboration will contribute to strengthening healthcare education and preparing a skilled workforce capable of supporting quality patient care.

For NCRTH, the agreement reinforces its role as a referral, teaching and training institution, while providing an opportunity to contribute to the development of future healthcare professionals and strengthen healthcare service delivery in Nakuru County.

The MKU delegation comprised Dr. Alfred Owino, Director of Nakuru Campus; Mr. Boniface Murigi, Director of Communication and Corporate Affairs; and Dr. John Kisengi of the School of Pharmacy.

The partnership reflects the shared commitment of MKU and its healthcare partners to strengthening university-industry collaboration, enhancing experiential learning and translating academic knowledge into meaningful impact on patient care and community health.

Through strategic partnerships with healthcare institutions, MKU continues to advance practical training and nurture the next generation of skilled healthcare professionals.

item.content:encoded:
Mount Kenya University (MKU) continues to contribute to national conversations on sustainable development and community resilience through the expertise of its academic and administrative leaders.

Dr. Gordon Ocholla, MKU Kisumu Centre Coordinator, was among the panelists at the 12th National Symposium for Disaster Risk Reduction, held from 10–12 October 2026 in Nakuru County, Kenya. Organised by the National Disaster Operations Centre (NDOC), the symposium was held under the theme “Resilience Starts at Home.” Where he joined national and international stakeholders in advancing inclusive, community-centred approaches to disaster preparedness and resilience.

The symposium brought together stakeholders from government, academia, civil society, and international development agencies, including the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP), the United Nations Population Fund (UNFPA), and other institutions working to strengthen disaster preparedness, response, and recovery.

Dr. Gordon participated in a panel discussion on Gender, Protection and Social Inclusion in Resilience Building, moderated by John Wafula of UNFPA. The discussion examined how disaster resilience initiatives can respond to the diverse needs, vulnerabilities, and lived experiences of different members of society.

The deliberations underscored the need to address structural inequalities that influence how communities prepare for, respond to, and recover from disasters. Participants also highlighted the importance of integrating protection, gender-based violence prevention, and sexual and reproductive health considerations into disaster management strategies.

The discussion further emphasised that women, children, persons with disabilities, and older persons should have meaningful roles in decision-making processes, while local communities should be recognised as key partners whose knowledge and priorities inform resilience planning.

Participants also called attention to the need for equitable financing, stronger accountability, and the allocation of resources to communities facing the greatest risks.

Reflecting on the discussions, Dr. Gordon emphasized that disaster resilience goes beyond recovering from emergencies. It also requires confronting the inequalities that determine who is most exposed to risk, who has the resources to cope, and whose voice is heard during recovery. His participation highlights the importance of bringing diverse professional perspectives and practical insights into national policy and development conversations.

For Mount Kenya University, the engagement reflects the value of sharing institutional expertise beyond the classroom and contributing to dialogue that addresses real-world challenges affecting communities.

Through the participation of its leaders in professional and national forums, MKU continues to support knowledge exchange, inclusive development, and solutions that contribute to more resilient communities.

Mount Kenya University supports the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) and serves as the United Nations Academic Impact Hub Chair for SDG 9: Industry, Innovation and Infrastructure for 2025–2027.

Dr. Ocholla’s contribution to discussions on gender, protection and social inclusion aligns with SDG 5: Gender Equality and SDG 10: Reduced Inequalities.

MKU also offers programmes that equip learners with skills relevant to gender advocacy, peacebuilding, security and governance, including the Bachelor of Arts in Justice and Security Studies, Bachelor of Arts in Peace Studies and Conflict Resolution, Bachelor of Arts in Public Administration and Governance, Diploma in Peace Studies and Conflict Resolution, and Diploma in Security Studies and Criminology.

item.content:encoded:
On 12th October, Mount Kenya University (MKU) hosted the Kenya Human Resource Students Association (KHRSA) Symposium at Mwai Kibaki Convention Centre, bringing together HR students, practitioners, employers, educators, and industry leaders under the theme “Building Kenya’s Future Workforce: Empowering the Next Generation of Human Resource.”

The symposium connected MKU students with practising HR leaders, offering valuable insights into industry realities, career development, and the importance of mentorship in shaping future professionals.

One of the participating HR leaders shared a powerful reminder:

“If you cannot see where you are going, ask someone who has been there before.” — J. Loren Norris

At MKU, we believe that the future of work begins with empowering the people who will lead it.

At MKU you can study:

  1. Doctor of Philosophy in Business Administration (Human Resource and Organizational management option)
  2. Masters of Science in Human Resource Development
  3. Bachelor of Business Management (Human Resource Management option)
  4. Diploma in Human Resource Management
  5. Certificate in Human Resource Management
  6. Certified Human Resource Professional (CHRP) offered through MKU Centre for professional development

#MKU #KHRSA #HumanResourceManagement #FutureOfWork #Mentorship #BuildingKenyaFutureWorkforce

The post MKU Hosts UN Lecture on Volunteerism and New Technologies. appeared first on Mount Kenya University.
item.content:encoded:
Public lecture explores how volunteerism and new technologies can help build peaceful, sustainable communities.

United Nations official Maher Nasser has urged governments and communities to confront climate change, rising inequality and the rapid growth of artificial intelligence through stronger global cooperation.
Nasser, Director of the Outreach Division at the United Nations Department of Global Communications, made the call while delivering the keynote address at a public lecture hosted by Mount Kenya University’s Institute of International Development Law and African Studies (IIDLAW) at its Parklands School of Law in Nairobi. MKU Vice-Chancellor Prof. Deogratius JAGANYI gave the welcoming remarks.

The lecture examined how volunteerism and new technologies can advance peace and sustainable development. It marked the International Year of Volunteers 2026 and highlighted the role of community action in achieving the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs).

Nasser pointed to Africa’s record in education and innovation, citing Morocco’s Al-Qarawiyyin and Egypt’s Al-Azhar as historic centres of learning. He also singled out Kenya’s M-Pesa as an innovation with influence beyond the country.

With the United Nations Volunteers programme marking 55 years, Nasser urged young people to take part in community service, saying volunteering helps build practical skills, strengthen communities and develop active global citizens.

Wairimu Kamau, a senior official at the State Department for Social Protection and Senior Citizen Affairs, said volunteer work can give young people practical experience, professional networks and skills valued in the workplace. She said technology can help recruit and train volunteers and track their impact, but stressed the need to protect personal data, widen access and bridge the digital divide.

Kamau praised MKU’s community service model and called on universities to make service hours part of their curricula. At MKU, student volunteers are taking on community challenges through the Millennium Fellowship, a global initiative supported by the United Nations Academic Impact. The programme trains students in project management and resource mobilisation. Over the past two years, MKU participants have led initiatives in healthcare, housing, education and other areas.

To sustain the work despite limited fellowship places and funding, the university community established the Millennium Campus Network Club. The Career Office and School of Social Sciences work with undergraduate students through the club to support SDG-focused volunteer projects.
Ian Mwangi, a 2025 fellowship beneficiary studying medicine at MKU’s Thika Campus, said the club connects current and former volunteers to mentor new participants, share resources and expand community initiatives.

Participants discussed using technology to strengthen volunteer work in health, education, disability inclusion and environmental conservation. Student leaders called for clearer guidance and greater access to formal recognition and global platforms to help volunteers build experience while serving their communities.

MKU’s hosting of Nasser was linked to its role as the United Nations Academic Impact SDG 9 Hub Chair for Industry, Innovation and Infrastructure. The five-year appointment runs from 2025 to 2030, with higher education institutions in Japan, Spain and Canada serving as vice-chairs.
